standard.title: Purpose and audience vary texts
standard.description: recognise how texts can be created for similar purposes but different audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify how similar topics and information are presented differently across text types (AC9E2LY01). They have not yet examined how the same purpose can produce different texts when the audience changes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise how texts created for similar purposes differ when aimed at different audiences.

nodes.label: Audience shapes text choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how texts with the same purpose are created differently for different audiences.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare two texts with the same purpose but different audiences (e.g. a safety campaign for adults vs children) and identify at least two ways the texts differ because of the audience.
nodes.typical_width: Identify how the same purpose (e.g. safety, instruction, persuasion) produces different texts for different audiences — examining vocabulary, images, examples and complexity as audience-driven choices.
wider: Compare instructions for assembling the same item written for different age groups, and discuss what specific changes are made to suit each audience
Find examples of similar-purpose texts aimed at children versus adults and evaluate whether the audience-related choices are effective

response_modes.reason: Students often see text differences as arbitrary or about topic rather than audience. Comparing texts with the same purpose but different audiences — across multiple examples — builds the insight that audience is a systematic determinant of textual choices.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least two specific differences between two texts with the same purpose
Student connects each difference to the audience — explaining why the audience requires that particular choice
